name: What happens if my bathroom remodel uncovers old plumbing that is not up to code?

mainEntity.name: How should homeowners handle outdated plumbing discovered after demolition begins?
mainEntity.text: How should homeowners handle outdated plumbing discovered after demolition begins?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older plumbing often becomes visible only after demolition. If the contractor finds corroded pipes, poor connections, or outdated shutoff valves, those items may need to be updated before the new finishes go in. That can affect both budget and timeline, but it is usually the right time to fix them because the wall cavities are already open. Homeowners should ask how the contractor handles added work, whether pricing is approved before changes are made, and whether the original quote included an allowance for unexpected plumbing repairs. This is one of the main reasons bathroom remodels can expand beyond the original plan. When the hidden systems are old, the project is not just about finishes anymore; it becomes a rebuild of the room’s infrastructure.
acceptedAnswer.description: If old plumbing is uncovered, the contractor may need to replace lines, fittings, or valves before the bathroom can be rebuilt. This can add cost and time, but it is usually better to correct unsafe or unreliable plumbing while the walls are open.
